questions.question: You ship a checkout modal. What accessibility checks do you run before release?
questions.title: Scenario — Accessible Checkout Modal Checklist
questions.direct_answer:
You ship a checkout modal. What accessibility checks do you run before release?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** End-to-end scenario thinking: focus trap, ESC, dialog roles, form errors, contrast, SR smoke test.

**Classic weak answer:** Letting focus fall behind the modal or leaving background scroll interactive.

**Senior finish:** Mention inert/aria-hidden on background, scroll lock, and reduced-motion preference.

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention inert/aria-hidden on background, scroll lock, and reduced-motion preference

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Scenario — Accessible Checkout Modal Checklist** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** You ship a checkout modal. What accessibility checks do you run before release?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **End-to-end scenario thinking: focus trap, ESC, dialog roles, form errors, contrast, SR smoke test**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Letting focus fall behind the modal or leaving background scroll interactive**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention inert/aria-hidden on background, scroll lock, and reduced-motion preference**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** End-to-end scenario thinking: focus trap, ESC, dialog roles, form errors, contrast, SR smoke test
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    NET[HTML + CSS + JS download] --> PARSE[Parse DOM + CSSOM]
    PARSE --> TREE[Render tree + layout]
    TREE --> PAINT[Paint + composite layers]
    PAINT --> LCP[LCP element timing]
    subgraph Perf["Performance hooks"]
        PRE[preload / prefetch]
        LAZY[lazy images + code-split]
    end
    NET --> PRE
    TREE --> LAZY
```

sections.title: Answer scaffold (what to cover vs what to avoid)
sections.content:
| Angle | What a strong answer includes |
|---|---|
| **What interviewers probe** | End-to-end scenario thinking: focus trap, ESC, dialog roles, form errors, contrast, SR smoke test |
| **Weak signal (avoid)** | Letting focus fall behind the modal or leaving background scroll interactive |
| **Differentiator** | Mention inert/aria-hidden on background, scroll lock, and reduced-motion preference |
| **Proof you shipped it** | Metrics (LCP, error rate), tests, DevTools trace, or incident story |

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **letting focus fall behind the modal or leaving background scroll interactive** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** End-to-end scenario thinking: focus trap, ESC, dialog roles, form errors, contrast, SR smoke test
- **Pitfall:** Letting focus fall behind the modal or leaving background scroll interactive
- **Differentiator:** Mention inert/aria-hidden on background, scroll lock, and reduced-motion preference
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **End-to-end scenario thinking: focus trap, ESC, dialog roles, form errors, contrast, SR smoke test** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Letting focus fall behind the modal or leaving background scroll interactive** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention inert/aria-hidden on background, scroll lock, and reduced-motion preference**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

followup_questions: How do you prevent background interaction while a modal is open?
What WCAG criteria apply to modals?
How do you handle a long checkout form in a modal?

questions.question: How do you make a large data table accessible?
questions.title: Scenario — Accessible Data Table Patterns
questions.direct_answer:
How do you make a large data table accessible?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Table semantics vs div grids, sticky headers, keyboard navigation in dense UIs.

**Classic weak answer:** Rebuilding tables with divs and losing column/row relationships.

**Senior finish:** Mention aria-sort on sortable columns and visually hidden text for trend icons.

interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention aria-sort on sortable columns and visually hidden text for trend icons
